newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Nine firms compete to advise on Cesp sale.
newsitem.headline: Nine firms compete to advise on Cesp sale.

text.p: Sao Paulo state government received proposals from nine consultants interested in advising it on the sale of power generating firm Cesp, officials said.

Two groups are bidding on the so-called A service contracts to evaluate Cesp's finances, said Ricardo Lima, an official at the Sao Paulo state Energy department who advises investors on the state's privatization plan.
Other seven groups are competing for the B service contracts, which includes financial evaluation, equity restructuring and the design of a privatization model for the firm, he added.

Lima noted that most of the groups that presented proposals to become Cesp's advisors also bid for contracts last week to advise on the sale of power distributors Companhia Paulista de Forca de Luz (CPFL) and Eletropaulo.
Winning bidders are expected to be announced by late February or early March and consultants will have 120 days to complete the evaluations,
The following groups bid on the A service contract:
* Group 1 - Grupo Trevisan, Arthur D. Little, BSB Engenharia and Banco Liberal;
* Group 2 - Banco Fator, Fator projeto, Azevedo Sodne, Ernst & Young, Themag and Paribas.
He also listed the groups competing for the B contract as follows:
* Group 1 - Banco Fator, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Azevedo Sodne, Ernest Young, Themag and Paribas.
* Group 2 - Graphus, Kleinwort Benson, CS First Boston, Unibanco and Engevix.
* Group 3 - Maxima, SBC Warburg, Morgan Stanley and Omega.
* Group 4 - Salomon Brothers, Banco Patrimonio and Schroder.
* Group 5 - J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Garantia and BVI.
* Group 6 - Bozano, Simonsen, BZW, Leman Brothers, Stone & Webster and Wald Associados.
* Group 7 - Projeto, Merrill Lynch, Rotchschild and ABN-Amro bank.
